### L1 review (#34704) · 2026-11-17T23:16Z

L1: ACCEPT
Head-sha: fbabe97b66860aaa9000cc70b171ae7491ba8a40

Tier H (`docs/adr/**`, 4 of 4 paths). This verdict does not ready the PR. It goes to the seat for its review and then to os-zhuang.

#### Must-fix
None.

#### Should-fix
None.

#### What I checked
- **Premise.** #31586 merged on 2026-11-08 at 21:16Z, merged by os-zhuang. Its squash commit is `5d1382a54c04968d7a1c39c1bb51a75c95cf7ea5`, dated 2026-11-08, so "on the day it was proposed" holds (the PR was opened at 16:10Z that day). The record's own sentence makes the maintainer's merge its acceptance, so `Accepted (2026-11-08, merged in #31586)` states a fact and does not add a ruling. `packages/cli/src/commands/lint.ts:186` already reads "ADR-0150 (accepted by merge, #31586)", which agrees.
- **The counts, against the record's own text at this head.**
  - The uncovered paragraph lists 11 types (sharing rule, queue, assignment rule, hook, job, app, page, dashboard, report, book, cube). Two of them (hook and job) change no bare answer, which leaves 9. So "For the other 9" (:350) is right, and so is "those 9 types" (:352), which refers back to it.
  - Phase 1 covers 13 `BARE_NAME_ONE_HOLDER_TYPES` plus permission sets, 14 in all (:404). So `B1…B14` (:393) is right.
  - #31586's own body ("of the 12 types phase 1 does not cover … the other 10", "13 per-type backstop narrowings") confirms how the counts went stale when `tool` joined phase 1 (#31414).
- **Scope.** The claim is 6963090735, and amendment 6963601898 covers ADR-0028's identical pointer and :352. Every edit stays inside a status line or one of the three counts. I compared each changed line word by word: no D1–D10 sentence, red line, quoted ruling or table-row content moves. Both earlier `Amended` entries are kept, the record does not say "implemented", and the new dated entry follows child A's practice of naming in-place rewrites on the status line.
- **ADR-0028 and ADR-0048.** Each changes only inside its existing ADR-0150 entry: `proposed` becomes `accepted`, and the conditional sentence becomes the dated fact. A repo-wide `git grep` at this head finds no other text that still calls ADR-0150 proposed or pending acceptance.
- **README.** It reads as regenerated output (Accepted 135→136, Proposed 8→7, the ADR-0150 row's status cell). CI's `check:adr-index` and the docs guards are green.
- **Shape.** `Fixes #34704`, Clause-② `no` and Metadata-protocol `none` match the claim. `skip-changeset` is right because no published package ships `docs/adr`. The body states only measured readings.
- **CI on this sha.** 50 runs: 27 success, 23 skipped, 0 failed, all completed. Mergeable: clean.

#### Notes
- N1: ":356, 'a refusal the maintainer scoped to 12 types'" is left as written, and I agree. That sentence reports what the maintainer scoped at the time, which was the 12 phase-1 types before `tool` joined. It is not arithmetic over the record's list.
- N2: the body's line numbers (:350, :352, :393, :404) match this head. The card's numbers (:348, :391, :402) were read on an older main, and the difference is only that drift.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `fbabe97b66860aaa9000cc70b171ae7491ba8a40`
Local-runs: none
Scope: docs/adr/0028-metadata-naming-and-namespace-isolation.md, docs/adr/0048-cross-package-metadata-collision.md, docs/adr/0150-behavioural-metadata-addressed-by-package-objects-keep-the-literal-prefix.md, docs/adr/README.md + none
Security-touching: no

PR #35013 (card #34704), net diff against `main` `4443014630` (the merge base is `main`'s tip): 4 files, +9/−9, all under `docs/adr/**`. Read: the card body and its four comments (triage 6941568113, claim 6963090735, dev report 6963570738, claim amendment 6963601898), the PR body, the file list, the word-level diff, and the check-runs on the head. Nothing was built or run.

### ① Derived judgments

- **No accept set and no public surface moves.** The diff holds no schema, no export, no code and no generated artifact other than the ADR index. Right.
- **The ADR status vocabulary.** ADR-0150's keyword goes from `Proposed` to `Accepted`. Both are in the vocabulary the index reads (`scripts/adr-index.mjs`), and the record stays parsed. Right.
- **The index counts.** Accepted 135 to 136 and Proposed 8 to 7, total 157 unchanged: exactly one record changes keyword. Right.
- **The index row.** The new status cell is 75 characters and ends in the ellipsis, as the old cell and the neighbouring rows do; `(2026-11-08, merged in #31586).` is rendered `— 2026-11-08, merged in #31586.` the same way `(2026-11-08).` was. It reads as generator output, not a hand edit. Right.
- **Gate verdicts, from the check-runs on this head.** Every run is completed; none failed or was cancelled. Success includes Lint · docs & code guards, Lint · repo & tooling gates, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, Check Documentation Links, Governed Surface Queue Guard, PR-body guards, Check Changeset, Check PR Size, Type Check (4 jobs) and Test Core. The rest are skipped by path filter.
- **One limit of those verdicts.** The CI `check:adr-index` step is report-only (the README's own first line: a stale index is a warning and never fails), so a green lint run does not prove the README is current. The README judgment above therefore rests on reading the three changed lines against the status line, and on the dev's recorded `node scripts/adr-index.mjs --check` exit 0 (comment 6963570738), which I did not re-run.

### ② Semver level

Clause-②: no — the diff publishes nothing. No published package ships `docs/adr`, so `skip-changeset` is the right carrier; the label is on the PR and Check Changeset is green. The PR body's `Clause-②: no` line and `Metadata-protocol: none` line match the claim and the tree.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: empty. Nothing to answer.
- **Deviation 1a, "those 10 types" (:352), not on the card.** Accepted. It refers back to "For the other 10" two lines above, and the claim amendment 6963601898 covers it.
- **Deviation 1b, ADR-0028's pointer, a file the card did not name.** Accepted. On `main` it carries the same conditional sentence as ADR-0048, word for word. Correcting one and not the other would leave two records disagreeing about one fact. The claim amendment adds the path.
- **Deviation 1c, the new dated `Amended` entry on ADR-0150's status line.** Accepted. It follows the record's own practice (the 2026-11-09 child A entry names in-place rewrites on the status line), and it says what changed without adding a ruling.
- **Deviation 6, text left as written.** Agreed. "no child lands before this record is accepted" (:3, :337) and the heading "Execution plan (after acceptance)" are rules and an anchor, and they still read true. Renaming the heading would break the `#execution-plan-after-acceptance` anchor the status line links to.
- **Out-of-scope finding, :356 "a refusal the maintainer scoped to 12 types".** Agreed that it stays. The text merged in #31586 said 12 when phase 1 covered 12 types, and what the maintainer scoped is not arithmetic over the record's list. It is not in this diff.
- **SQL push-down.** Not applicable: no code.
- **Security.** No changed hunk teaches permission, sharing, credential, token or authentication behaviour. The B row names `security-catalog-namespace.ts`, but only its label (`B1…B13` to `B1…B14`) changes.

### ④ Design judgment

No must-fix, no should-fix.

**Is every changed line a status, count or pointer correction?** Yes. I read the word-level diff of all nine changed lines.

- ADR-0150 :3 changes the keyword and date clause, turns "becomes … by the maintainer's merge" into "became … by the maintainer's merge of #31586 (commit `5d1382a54c`), on the day it was proposed", and appends one `Amended (2026-11-17, #34704)` entry. The epic-ruling clause, the ⛔ sentence, "This record declares; it implements nothing", the supersedes, amends and withdraws clauses, and both earlier `Amended` entries are byte-identical.
- ADR-0150 :350 and :352 change `10` to `9` and nothing else. :393 changes the row label only; the row's five other cells are identical.
- ADR-0028 :3 and ADR-0048 :3 change, inside their existing ADR-0150 entry only, `(proposed` to `(accepted` and the conditional last sentence to the dated fact. The ruled content of each entry (which decisions are adopted, what retires, what stays) is identical.
- No D1–D10 sentence, red line, quoted ruling or table-row content moves. The record does not say "implemented".

**Is "Accepted" the right status?** Yes, on four independent readings.

- The record's own rule on `main`: "this record becomes **Accepted** by the maintainer's merge". #31586 is merged, `merged_by` os-zhuang, at 2026-11-08T21:16:33Z, merge commit `5d1382a54c04968d7a1c39c1bb51a75c95cf7ea5` (GitHub compare: the head is ahead of that commit, behind by 0). `.github/CODEOWNERS` names os-zhuang as the Tier H approver.
- The repo's rule: AGENTS.md Prime Directive 14 lands a Tier H surface "by the maintainer's hand (merge or enqueue)". The registry's precedent says the same in words: ADR-0125 is "accepted by the merge that landed it on `main` …, which is itself the acceptance act for a governed surface", and ADR-0130, 0131, 0132, 0133 and 0139 use the same form.
- The tree already acts on the acceptance. ADR-0150's 2026-11-09 entry speaks of rulings "recorded on the children since acceptance"; children have landed (P #31669, G1 #31691) under a rule that none lands before acceptance; `packages/cli/src/commands/lint.ts:186` reads "ADR-0150 (accepted by merge, #31586)".
- The status-hygiene convention in the README reserves `Accepted — implemented` for a record whose implementation has landed. Children are still in flight, so plain `Accepted` is the correct keyword and the PR is right not to go further.

"On the day it was proposed" holds in UTC: the PR opened at 16:10Z and merged at 21:16Z on 2026-11-08, and the record's `Date` is 2026-11-08.

**Are the counts right?** Yes, against the record at this head and at its first text (`5d1382a54c`).

- Uncovered types (:346): sharing rule, queue, assignment rule, hook, job, app, page, dashboard, report, book, cube. That is 11, as the sentence says. Hook and job change no bare answer, which leaves 9. So "For the other 9" and "those 9 types" are right.
- B children: `BARE_NAME_ONE_HOLDER_TYPES` lists 13 (picklist, mapping, dataset, api, the object-less action, function, flow, webhook, connector, email_template, agent, skill, tool) plus permission sets, 14. The record says "14 types phase 1 covers" (:341) and "14 in all" (:404). So `B1…B14` is right.
- How they went stale: the first text read "The other 12 … and tool", "the other 10", "those 10", `B1…B13` and "13 in all". When `tool` joined phase 1 (#31414), child A rewrote 12 to 11 and 13 to 14 and left the three dependent counts. The new `Amended` entry states exactly this, and it is accurate.

**Tried to break it.**

- Other text still calling ADR-0150 proposed or pending: a grep of `docs`, `content`, `skills`, `packages` and `.claude` at the head finds none. No "takes effect when", `B1…B13`, "other 10" or "those 10" is left under `docs`.
- The new ADR-0028 and ADR-0048 sentences each name #31586 as a bare number, as the neighbouring entries do; Check Documentation Links and the ADR anchor gates are green.
- The first consumer of the status line is the index generator: it reads `Accepted` as the keyword and the row and summary follow.

**Nits and observations (none affects correctness or the contract).**

- N1 (nit) — the new `Amended` entry says "two counts … are corrected" and then names three edited places. It is accurate (two counts, one of them written twice), and may stay as written.
- O1 (outside the diff, not reviewed) — ADR-0141 and ADR-0153 carry the same "becomes **Accepted** by the maintainer's merge" sentence, are on `main`, and still read `Proposed`. ADR-0141 is already cited and superseded in part by later records. Whether each is stale the same way depends on who merged it; that is a census for a follow-up card, not for this PR.
- O2 — :356 "scoped to 12 types": see ③. A maintainer question if anyone wants it changed.
